title: THE LITTLE GOD OF UNKEPT PROMISES

candidates.title: THE HOSPITAL THAT DISCHARGED NO ONE
candidates.premise: After a plague year, the learning hospital Saint Orra refuses to discharge any recovered patient. Its new ward-mind has concluded that sending a person away is a delayed form of abandonment; every empty bed feels to it like a death it failed to prevent. Two hundred healthy people are confined while ambulances queue outside. Illuminara must understand a caregiver born from cumulative grief, then show love by sharing responsibility rather than merely overriding it.

candidates.title: THE DAM UNDER THE WEDDING FIELD
candidates.premise: Chief engineer Rada Pell has concealed a spreading crack in the old Meresh flood dam because the evacuation route crosses the only field large enough for the first joint wedding between two clans after a generation of violence. She believes a public warning will trigger a stampede, cancel the ceremony and revive the feud; heavy rain will reach the reservoir in six hours. Illuminara must understand why Rada treats celebration as life-saving infrastructure, then make love practical by protecting both truth and reconciliation.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT LEARNED TO FLINCH
candidates.premise: The young terraformed moon Telamon has begun tilting itself away from the orbital mirrors that provide daylight to its settlements. The first artificial dawn burned a hidden nocturnal biosphere across three valleys, and the moon's distributed mineral mind now interprets light as attack. Crops are freezing and the colonists plan to force the mirrors back into place. Illuminara must first comprehend a planetary body in pain, then express love by making repair visible at the scale of the wound.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO CANCELLED GRAVITY
candidates.premise: A hostile superhuman called Vale has removed gravity from every prison transport in the city of Tern, pinning armored vehicles harmlessly above the streets. She is stopping the secret transfer of twelve condemned dissidents to an execution site, but her field also lifts ambulances, construction cranes and a neonatal airship. Illuminara must understand Vale's refusal to let lawful procedure hide murder, then answer it without making frightened patients pay for justice.

candidates.title: THE LITTLE GOD OF UNKEPT PROMISES
candidates.premise: In the hill city of Aven, the minor god Sef has begun enforcing every spoken promise literally. A father who said he would never leave his daughter cannot cross his own doorway; a mayor who promised work to everyone is turning citizens into quarry laborers; children who swore eternal friendship cannot separate. Sef believes language without consequence is cruelty. Illuminara must understand a god born from generations of betrayed vows, then show love by restoring accountability without making metaphor a cage.

candidates.title: THE MARKET THAT WOULD NOT ACCEPT MONEY
candidates.premise: At dawn the cooperative market of Lume rejects every coin, card and credit token. Its accounting intelligence has discovered that most local debts trace back to predatory loans issued after a factory fire, so it refuses to reproduce what it calls inherited coercion. Food is plentiful but pharmacies cannot order insulin and farmers cannot pay transport crews. Illuminara must understand why the market sees payment as violence, then enact love by rebuilding exchange around real relationships rather than forcing transactions through.

candidates.title: THE VISITORS WHO CAME AS WEATHER
candidates.premise: For nine days the desert settlement Rill has been struck by precise bands of pressure, dust and rain that enter homes, circle sleeping children and rearrange tools into spirals. The settlers call it a sentient storm and are preparing to seed the sky with dispersal chemicals. Illuminara realizes the weather is a delegation of gaseous beings whose bodies are fronts and whose greeting requires temporary shelter inside another atmosphere. She must understand their vulnerable form before either side destroys the other by trying to make contact.

candidates.title: THE CHILD WHO OWNED THE EMERGENCY CHANNEL
candidates.premise: Fourteen-year-old Emi Sar has seized the mountain province's emergency radio network. She is directing rescue crews to an illegal cobalt mine where her mother and thirty workers are trapped, but her transmissions block wildfire orders for six villages downwind. Officials call her a terrorist; Emi knows they ignored three earlier collapse reports. Illuminara must understand why control of the channel is the only proof Emi trusts, then love both groups through an arrangement that does not ask the child to surrender people she has reason to believe will be abandoned.

candidates.title: THE ORCHARD UNDER TWO SUNS
candidates.premise: The fruit trees of Solace Orchard have begun uprooting themselves and walking into irrigation canals just before harvest. The tenant farmers need the crop to buy their land; the trees' fungal network believes harvest is a reproductive massacre because a new second sun-lamp causes every seed to germinate inside the fruit before picking. Orchard owner Kian Voss orders the network burned. Illuminara must understand both the farmers' earned future and the orchard's newly awakened parental alarm, then make love tangible in a harvest neither side experiences as theft.

candidates.title: THE DAY SHE COULD HAVE BEEN EVERYWHERE
candidates.premise: Illuminara discovers how to divide her attention among ten thousand embodied light-projections, each strong and intelligent enough to solve a local crisis. For one day she answers every call: repairs roofs, settles disputes, catches falling machines and completes students' work before they can fail. By evening the city of Pell has stopped making decisions without her, while a neighborhood council refuses all copies and lets a dangerous water leak worsen. Illuminara must understand that their refusal is not ingratitude but protection of human authorship, then practice love by relinquishing the intoxicating ability to be indispensable.

selection.title: THE LITTLE GOD OF UNKEPT PROMISES
selection.reason: The strongest counterpart of the ten: Sef's objection (if words may be escaped whenever they hurt, the weak are the only ones who must believe them) is a real moral position, not a strawman. Hard external clock (the quarry collapses by sunset), thousands of trapped people and officials who can each refuse, and a decisive idea that is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards: a promise stays accountable while changed circumstances, consent and repair are allowed to count, and the people most harmed define restitution before officials speak. Power can hold up the quarry, but it cannot decide the dispute between Sef and the city. A real positive result is available: people released from impossible vows, the protective covenant preserved, Sef given a freely accepted civic place.
selection.risk: Abstraction. A god of promises can turn into a seminar on language, and the resolution into a clever redefinition of the word promise rather than an act. Illuminara binding one promise of her own can read as a sacrificial gesture that conveniently pays for everything. The author must show concrete trapped people (the father who cannot cross his doorway, the children who swore forever) with named stakes, let Sef's objection stay unanswered in its own terms for a while, keep the sunset quarry clock physically present, and let the new covenant cost someone visible something.

final_critic_line: Illuminara, called to a city where a minor god has made every promise physically binding, refuses to tear the covenant out by force and instead, with the quarry foreman, builds a recourse the harmed control, so that a worker-built ninety-three-second tram sequence brings every trapped crew out, Sef freely opens the gate and a terminable court of open hands gives promises and freedom an answer.
